rationale: Assigned Labour Market & Employment because the substantive object is occupational mobility into creative work, studied via the ONS Longitudinal Study 1971-2021; Life-Course / Trajectory Analysis because social mobility into an occupation is followed longitudinally across cohorts over a fifty-year span; no tag because the mobility comparison is socioeconomic rather than centred on a demographic or equality-relevant group.

Title: Educational differentiation and intergenertional mobility
Datasets Used: Office for National Statistics: Longitudinal Education Outcomes
rationale: Assigned Education & Skills and Labour Market & Employment because educational differentiation and its link to intergenerational mobility is studied via Longitudinal Education Outcomes, which links education records to earnings; Life-Course / Trajectory Analysis because intergenerational mobility follows progression from education into adult economic position across generations; no tag because no demographic-equity or pandemic lens is central.

Title: Characterisation of non-resident parents: Exploring Patterns of Parental Arrangements, Contact, and Engagement in Early Childhood in the Children of 2020s birth cohort study
Datasets Used: Office for the National Statistics: Children of the 2020s: Wave 1
rationale: Assigned Migration & Demographics because the substantive object is family structure and non-resident parental arrangements, a demographic-composition question studied in the Children of the 2020s birth cohort; Descriptive Monitoring because the title's 'characterisation' and 'exploring patterns' indicate profiling arrangements, contact and engagement rather than testing effects; no tag because demographic variables describe the study population rather than a central equity comparison.

Title: Driving Business Productivity in Northern Ireland
Datasets Used:
Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency:
Northern Ireland Annual Business Inquiry (NIABI),
Northern Ireland Economic Trade Statistics (NIETS)
Northern Ireland Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings (NI ASHE)
Office for National Statistics: Business Register and Employment Survey, Annual Business Survey, Business Register and Employment Survey, Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings, Employer Skills Survey and Investment in Training, Business Structure Database, Management and Expectations Survey
rationale: Assigned Business & Productivity because firm productivity in Northern Ireland is the substantive object, evidenced by business surveys including the NI Annual Business Inquiry, Business Structure Database and Annual Business Survey; Outcome Tracking because 'driving' productivity indicates linking firm characteristics such as skills, training and trade (Employer Skills Survey, trade statistics) to productivity outcomes rather than evaluating a named policy; no tag because no pandemic or demographic-equity lens is evident.

Title: National Living Wage and firm productivity
Datasets Used: Office for National Statistics: Business Structure Database, Business Register Employment Survey, Longitudinal Small Business Survey, Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings, Business Enterprise Research and Development, Longitudinal Inter-Departmental Business Register, Annual Business Survey
rationale: Assigned Business & Productivity and Labour Market & Employment because the project studies firm productivity responses to a wage-floor policy, using business surveys and the Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings; Policy Evaluation / Impact Analysis because the National Living Wage is a named policy whose impact on firms is being evaluated; no tag because no demographic-equity or pandemic lens is central.
